stages.label: Extraction
stages.description: Locate the sources of primary material.
stages.scope: Oil/gas production is upstream context. These sources cannot identify which output becomes plastic rather than fuel.

stages.label: Refining
stages.description: Find where raw inputs are separated, purified or transformed.
stages.scope: Petrochemical cracking produces chemical feedstocks. Plant outputs are not all plastic, and supply links to manufacturers are not provided.

stages.label: Making products
stages.description: See where materials become industrial products.
stages.scope: Final product makers are not comprehensively identified in the retained sources. Customs product records do not locate the factories.

stages.label: Use
stages.description: Find industrial users and examine national material accounts.
stages.scope: Households, buildings and individual product use are not geolocated by these datasets. National consumption accounts describe broader material demand.

stages.label: Recovery
stages.description: Locate infrastructure that may return discarded material to use.
stages.scope: General recycling and material-recovery infrastructure. Accepted materials and actual recovery outcomes vary; these are not verified destinations for this material.

stages.label: Disposal
stages.description: See infrastructure where residual waste is deposited.
stages.scope: General solid-waste disposal infrastructure, shown as context. The source does not establish that a selected product or material reaches these sites.

stages.label: To the ocean
stages.description: Compare modeled river-borne plastic releases at river mouths.
stages.scope: Meijer et al. model of river plastic emissions for 2015. Outfalls are modeled release locations; they do not trace a selected object or identify upstream suppliers.

method: Filtered source types from the validated facility inventory. Dates, coordinates, source IDs and detail-chunk links are unchanged. No geographic proximity links, shipment tracking, interpolation or unique-facility deduplication is applied.
